data_check.notes: Reads were formed from script and matchup before checking recent production against the lines. Barner's 101 yards over three games equals 33.7 per game, with 5.7 targets per game and 5.94 yards per target; at that historical efficiency, five targets correspond to approximately 29.7 yards, only modestly above 27.5. Waddle's 64 yards over three games equals 21.3 per game and 3.37 yards per target. Even a hypothetical rebound to 5.5 yards per target on eight targets produces 44 yards, but this is a sensitivity check, not a fitted projection. SEA's five-game passing-location and explosive-play numbers support, rather than contradict, the Waddle read. Neither recent average is treated as a stand-alone edge or calibrated win probability.

pre_mortem: Barner: It is Monday and the over lost because Denver's middle-field allowance did not describe Barner's actual routes. Seattle ran successfully against the defense allowing 4.91 YPC, or Smith-Njigba absorbed the passing volume; Barner's short air-yard profile then required catches and yards after catch that never arrived. Waddle: The under lost because his recent 3.37 yards per target reflected temporary inefficiency rather than a stable limitation. Nineteen targets and 134 air yards still provide opportunity, Seattle blitzes only 21%, and DEN's supplied QB performance improves from -0.27 EPA/dropback against blitzes to 0.01 otherwise. A modest volume increase or explosive reception can erase the apparent cushion. Both remain leans because these counter-cases are material and player availability is unverified.
